source.title: SAeUron: Interpretable Concept Unlearning in Diffusion Models with Sparse Autoencoders

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates whether SAE features correspond to interpretable concepts and reports limits: features overlap for similar concepts, and the method performs poorly on abstract concepts. It does not test superposition or capacity competition directly.
record.gate_note: The study uses SAEs to identify and intervene on features in diffusion models, not to test whether networks store more features than dimensions, whether superposition geometry depends on sparsity or importance, or whether polysemanticity reflects capacity pressure. Its feature-alignment and failure-case results bear on V5, but it does not test feature stability or establish that SAE features are complete or canonical units. Results about competing unlearning methods and cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper uses SAEs as a tool for concept unlearning in Stable Diffusion and mainly reports its own method's performance (UnlearnCanvas, I2P, adversarial robustness). Its interpretability checks (kNN probes, activation heatmaps, steering) show that selected SAE features in a diffusion U-Net match visual concepts. They do not test whether features outnumber dimensions, capacity competition, the causes of polysemanticity, LLM feature spread, or SAE features' completeness, stability or canonicality. The subject is a diffusion model, not an LLM, so V4 does not apply.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. In addition, the authors claim SOTA unlearning on UnlearnCanvas, effective nudity removal, multi-concept unlearning and adversarial robustness. They attribute the limits on similar and abstract concepts to SAE features that capture visual elements.
record.recipe_differences: This is an SAE-based inference-time unlearning method for text-to-image diffusion models, not a reproduction of toy-model superposition experiments; it selects and blocks concept-associated SAE features.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome depends on concept type and similarity: the authors report overlap and collateral degradation for similar classes, and weaker performance for abstract concepts. Feature activity and score distributions also vary across denoising timesteps.

fits_no_version.finding: SAEs (BatchTopK, 16x expansion) trained on Stable Diffusion cross-attention activations yield features whose selected members match objects, styles and object parts. Evidence: kNN probes above chance, heatmaps, steering, GPT-4o annotations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs recover concept-interpretable sparse features in text-to-image diffusion models.

fits_no_version.finding: Similar classes (Cats/Dogs) share a selected head-related feature in early timesteps. The authors also say SAE features correspond to visual parts, so abstract concepts (hate, violence) are poorly captured.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Diffusion-model SAE features are visual-part-level and do not isolate abstract or highly similar concepts.

record.problems: The feature-classification results are presented in figures without numeric values in the text. The paper does not measure feature stability or dictionary completeness, and reports limitations for similar and abstract concepts. The abstract-category benchmark uses a detector-based measure.
record.rows_left_out: Other outcome metrics and comparisons for style/object unlearning, nudity unlearning, multi-concept unlearning, adversarial attacks, and quality were omitted because they report task performance rather than testing whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units (§5.3–6.2; Tables 1–2, 7; Figures 7, 9).

untested.parts: All: toy models, feature count vs dimensions, sparsity transition, geometry.
All: capacity competition as the cause of polysemanticity.
All: no LLMs are studied. The SAE feature recovery shown is in a diffusion U-Net.
Completeness, stability across runs or seeds, canonicality. Only the interpretability of score-selected features is shown.
All: no test of whether features are 1-D or multi-dimensional.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V5 labels are dropped: the study is a method paper (T4). None of its rows measure completeness, stability or canonicality of SAE units. The I2P rows are the study's own method's task performance, not version effects.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, feature-count versus dimension, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transition, and regular geometry.
Whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or important features receiving dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises for other reasons and whether it is evidence of superposition.
The experiments are on diffusion models, not LLMs; the study does not measure LLM features spread across neurons or SAE recovery in LLMs.

The study examines semantic correspondence and some feature overlap, but does not measure feature stability across models, training runs, or settings, nor establish completeness or canonicality of SAE features.
Although SAE features are represented by decoder directions, the study does not test whether underlying features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion v1.5
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned on the selected objects and styles from the UnlearnCanvas benchmark
rows.operation_detail: Visualized activations of score-selected SAE features on image patches to assess concept correspondence.

conditions.value: up.1.2 for styles; up.1.1 for objects

rows.measure: Qualitative correspondence between feature activations and visual concept regions
rows.value: The text reports that style features activate on characteristic style patterns, while object features activate on the target object across styles; style features can focus on backgrounds and ignore object regions.
rows.note: Supports concept-level interpretability in the illustrated settings, but does not establish completeness, stability, or canonicality.
rows.check: The heatmaps show that score-selected features match styles and objects in a diffusion model. That is interpretability of selected features, not completeness, stability or canonicality (V5). The subject is not an LLM (V4).

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion v1.5
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned on the selected objects and styles from the UnlearnCanvas benchmark
rows.operation_detail: Trained a 5-nearest-neighbors classifier on SAE feature activations from the unconditional generation part.
rows.note: The text says score-selected features achieve high accuracy across most timesteps and random features significantly outperform random guess, but gives no numeric values; this probe does not establish that features are complete or canonical.
rows.check: The kNN probe validates the authors' own feature selection and reads from a figure only. It does not measure V5's properties, and the subject is not an LLM.

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion v1.5
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned on the selected objects and styles from the UnlearnCanvas benchmark
rows.operation_detail: Trained a 5-nearest-neighbors classifier on SAE feature activations for style classification.
rows.note: The text says accuracy is similar using all features and score-selected features and tends to increase from approximately the 30-th timestep; no numeric values are stated.
rows.check: Same as r2, for style classification (Figure 16); no numbers are given.

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion v1.5
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned on the selected objects and styles from the UnlearnCanvas benchmark
rows.operation_detail: Added positive activation contributions along score-selected SAE feature decoder directions during unconditional generation.
rows.measure: Whether generated images visibly exhibit the selected style
rows.value: The text reports that steering produces generations with visual attributes corresponding to the selected styles.
rows.note: Shows a causal effect for selected features in these examples, not that the dictionary exhaustively or canonically represents the model.
rows.check: Qualitative steering examples show selected features have causal effects. This says nothing about whether the dictionary is complete or canonical.

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion v1.5
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned on the selected objects and styles from the UnlearnCanvas benchmark
rows.operation_detail: Compared features selected for cat and dog unlearning and examined generated images when either class was unlearned.

conditions.value: overlap occurs during the first 10 denoising timesteps

rows.measure: Overlap of selected features and degradation to the other class
rows.value: The text reports one feature selected for both classes during the first 10 denoising timesteps; unlearning one class can degrade the other, especially Dogs when Cats are unlearned.
rows.note: The authors identify an overlapping feature related to generating both animals’ heads.
rows.check: The Cats/Dogs overlap concerns which features the method selects. One shared head feature (17704) appears in early timesteps. This is a method failure case, not a test of whether SAE units are canonical.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Illustrated concept-feature alignment and steering examples
reader_labels.reason: Selected features align with recognizable visual patterns and steering produces corresponding styles, but these results do not establish complete, stable, canonical model units (r1–r4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Similar concepts and abstract inappropriate-content categories
reader_labels.reason: The authors report feature overlap and cross-class degradation for Cats and Dogs, and several abstract categories show no improvement over the SD baseline; this limits the scope of concept-specific SAE units (r5–r12).
